$$f(n)\equiv 2^{z(n)}\prod_{\text{digits }d}f(d)\pmod{10},\qquad z(n)=\frac{n-s_5(n)}4,$$
we get
$$f(5^an)\equiv f(n)\cdot 2^{(5^a-1)n/4}\pmod{10}.$$
For $n\ge2$, $f(n)$ is even, and multiplying an even digit by $6$ leaves it unchanged mod $10$. Hence we need $2^{(5^a-1)n/4}\equiv6\pmod{10}$ (i.e. the exponent is a positive multiple of $4$) for every $n$. This requires $(5^a-1)n/4\equiv0\pmod4$ for all $n$, which forces $5^a\equiv1\pmod{16}$. Since $5$ has order $4$ modulo $16$, we must have $4\mid a$.

One also checks that no $k$ having a factor coprime to $5$ can satisfy the condition (the base-5 digit-product term cannot be compensated by the power-of-$2$ factor for all $n$). Thus the complete list of solutions is
$$k=5^{4t}\quad(t=0,1,2,\dots).$$

In increasing order:

- 5th: $5^{16}=152\,587\,890\,625$

The number of decimal digits of $5^{16}$ is
$$\left\lfloor 16\log_{10}5\right\rfloor+1=\lfloor11.1835\ldots\rfloor+1=12.$$
